question: What is the main goal of triage in a busy emergency department?

options.A: Registering patient names and hospital cards
options.B: Sorting patients based on injury severity
options.C: Determining who arrived first at the hospital

explanation: You've got this! Triage simply means sorting patients by how critical their condition is, ensuring the sickest people get help right away. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h1)

question: Why do we treat triage as a continuous process rather than a one-time check in the emergency unit?

options.A: Hospital management requires hourly admission reports
options.B: Patients can deteriorate while waiting for care
options.D: Doctors change shifts every few hours

explanation: Well done! A patient who looks stable now can suddenly crash in the waiting area. Re-triage helps us catch those changes early. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h1)

question: What does the letter 'D' stand for in the ABCDE primary survey?
explanation: Disability checks the patient's basic neurological status and level of consciousness during the primary survey. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h2)

question: Why must emergency nurses follow the strict ABCDE order during a primary survey?

options.A: To address the most immediately fatal issues first
options.B: Because doctors prefer medical notes written this way
options.C: To make patient registration faster for clerks
options.D: It is required only for surgical trauma cases

explanation: Great thinking! The ABCDE rule ensures we tackle life-threatening breathing or circulation issues before anything else. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h2)

question: Which airway maneuver is safest to use when opening the airway of a suspected trauma patient?
explanation: Spot on! The jaw-thrust opens the airway without moving the neck, protecting the spine if there's a potential injury. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h3)

question: A patient with a blocked airway is making gurgling sounds from excess secretions. What is your immediate action?
explanation: You nailed it! Gurgling means fluid is trapped in the airway, so grabbing the suction machine right away clears the passage. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h3)

question: Which clinical sign is an early indicator of developing shock?
explanation: The body compensates for falling perfusion by increasing the heart rate, making tachycardia an early warning sign of shock. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h4)

question: Why is it dangerous to give large, rapid IV fluid volumes to a patient in cardiogenic shock?

options.A: Lowering the patient's body temperature too fast
options.D: Worsening pulmonary edema and heart failure

explanation: Brilliant! If the heart is already too weak to pump properly, extra fluid will just back up into the lungs and make things worse. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h4)

question: What does the letter 'A' stand for in the SAMPLE history mnemonic?
explanation: Allergies check for known drug or food reactions before any emergency medications are given. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h5)

question: When is the right time to start a secondary survey on an emergency patient?

options.A: Only after the patient is discharged to the ward
options.B: Before checking the airway or breathing status
options.C: Immediately upon the patient entering the door
options.D: After primary survey life threats are managed

explanation: Exactly! We only move to the secondary, head-to-toe check after we are sure the ABCs are stable. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h5)

question: During a cardiac arrest, which drug route is used for fast absorption when an IV line fails?
explanation: Spot on! Intraosseous (bone marrow) access lets emergency drugs enter the bloodstream almost as fast as a drip. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h6)

question: Why do nurses perform a double-check before giving high-alert emergency medications?

options.A: To prevent dangerous medication dosage errors
options.B: To replace the need for patient wristbands
options.C: To comply with hospital billing departments
options.D: To slow down the emergency nursing team

explanation: Well done! High-alert drugs have little room for error, so having a second pair of eyes keeps the patient safe. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h6)

question: What does closed-loop communication mean during a busy resuscitation?

options.A: Speaking in a whisper so family members cannot hear
options.B: Repeating an order back to confirm it was understood
options.C: Writing down clinical notes at the end of the shift
options.D: Using encrypted walkie-talkies across hospital departments

explanation: You've got this! Repeating an instruction back to the team leader ensures everyone is on the same page during a crisis. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h7)

question: Which action is a key part of Crisis Resource Management in an emergency nursing team?

options.A: Working in silence to maintain absolute focus
options.B: Waiting for senior doctors before starting CPR
options.C: Assigning clear roles to every team member
options.D: Allowing team members to switch tasks randomly

explanation: Spot on! Giving everyone a specific job prevents chaos and saves precious seconds in an emergency. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h7)

question: How do we handle consent when an unconscious trauma patient needs emergency life-saving surgery?

options.A: The nurse must sign financial guarantee forms first
options.B: Consent is legally implied in emergency situations
options.C: Treatment must wait until family arrives from afar
options.D: A court order must be obtained before touching them

explanation: Exactly! The law assumes an unconscious person would want us to save their life, so we can treat them immediately. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when documenting emergency care?

options.A: Documenting patient responses to resuscitation efforts
options.B: Waiting until the end of the week to write notes from memory
options.C: Recording exact times for every medication given
options.D: Writing contemporaneous notes during or right after care

explanation: You nailed it! Memories fade fast in emergencies, so waiting days to write notes is unsafe and legally risky. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h8)
